The Physics of Microbial Ecosystems (PoME) group - lab handbook Oliver Meacock 2026-08-25 Welcome! Welcome to the Physics of Microbial Ecosystems (PoME) group! This handbook is intended as your complete guide to life in your new position. If you find it is not a complete guide, please email Oli at o.meacock [at] sheffield.ac.uk with suggestions for additions. Assuming you have access to the School of Biosciences intranet, a lot of useful information can be found here. If youve not made it that far, check Section 6 first. You may also find what you are looking for on the group website.

Section 2 Where are we? We are based in the School of Biosciences, a component of the Faculty of Sciences. The school is a large complex of buildings at the heart of the University and hosts five research clusters: Molecular Microbiology: Biochemistry to Disease (MMBD) (where we are based) Ecology and Evolutionary Biology (EEB) (Good source of collaborations) Development, Regeneration and Neurophysiology (DRN) Molecular and Cellular Biology (MCB) Plants, Photosynthesis and Soil (PPS) We are based in the oldest part of the University, Firth Court (FC). Other buildings that make up the complex are the Florey, Perak, Addison, Edwardian and Alfred Denny (AD) buildings. Of these, the AD building most important to know about as it contains the lecture theatres where Biosciences seminars are held - you can access these by exiting FC from the front, taking the stairs down on your left and reentering the complex through the entrance immediately on your left. Needless to say there are many other routes but these will be left as an opportunity for exploration of the Biosciences rat nest! Some room numbers in the complex which may be of use: F21: Our lab space (shared with Laia Pasquina-Lemonche) F18: The lab space of Simon Foster - contains lots of communal equipment in frequent use by the group G05: Olis office

Section 3 Whats on the schedule? 3.1 Group meetings 3.1.1 Joint group meetings MMBD holds two multi-group research meetings between 10-11am every second week, one on alternating Wednesdays and one on alternating Fridays. The Wednesday sessions are attended by Graham Stafford, Ian Lidbury, Stephane Mesnage, Oliver Meacock and Laia Pasquina-Lemonche. They tend to be focused on cell wall biology, phages and environmental microbiology. The Friday sessions are attended by Per Bullough, Robert Fagan, Andrew Fenton, Mack Durham, Jason Wilson and Laia Pasquina-Lemonche and are more oriented towards pathogens, pathogensis and structural biology. 3.1.2 PoME meetings We hold meetings within PoME once a month at present. 3.2 Seminar series A complete list of seminars held in the School is available here. Key ones are the EEB and MMBD seminars, which are held at 1-2pm on Tuesdays and Thursdays respectively. Both internal and external speakers speak at these seminars. Another event to keep an eye out for is the Margaret Savigear lecture, which is an annual seminar specifically focused on female role models in science. These typically attract quite high profile scientists. 3.3 Cluster meetings MMBD holds cluster-wide meetings at 4pm on the first Friday of every month. These are predominantly meant for PIs in the cluster, but other cluster members are welcome to join. As well as administrative matters, these meetings are an opportunity for cluster members to pitch new grant or paper ideas to a reasonably generous audience. If you are interested in putting together a fellowship application (see chapter X) this is a good forum to get feedback on your idea at an early stage of development. 3.4 Social stuff EEB holds coffee and news mornings every Tuesday at 10:30-11:00 am in the Alfred Denny common room. There are also coffee mornings organised by the PGR committee and postdoc committee 10:30-11 on Wednesdays and Fridays respectively. These are either held in the Alfred Denny common room or the Addison common room (you will get emails telling you which one). MMBD PIs typically migrate to the university pub (the Uni Arms) after cluster meetings, while EEB members tend to start gathering there at about 5pm every week. Less frequent social events include the MMBD Christmas hike and the EEB Summer picnic.

Section 8 Career development This page will mostly focus on academic career development. For advice about transitioning into a non-academic career path, you may wish to get in touch with the Universitys career center. Alternatively, for researchers interested in translating their findings into real world applications, the knowledge exchange team would be a good point of contact. The academic career path is broadly PhD -> postdoc -> independent group leader. Each of these points of transition can be quite competitive, requiring evidence of high-quality outcomes at previous stages. 8.1 Fellowships Independent fellowships can be a big boost to your progress. These are parcels of money that are awarded to you as an individual on the basis of your proven track record and an excellent research proposal. These are available at all career stages, but the most critical are the transition to independence fellowships (typically pursued after a few years of postdoctoral experience). Such fellowships are now often the only route to a permanent job at UK research universities. Regardless of the career stage that is being applied for, you will need to be able to answer three key questions: What is the project? Why am I the best person to carry it out? Why is my chosen institution/group the best place to carry it out? If you can answer all three of those questions convincingly, you may be ready to apply. For those interested, this page provides further details on the schemes that Sheffield supports. I would be very happy to discuss ideas with you, although a critical factor in succeeding in such schemes is that your ideas are clearly distinctive from other peoples. The degree of independent idea development depends on your career stage, increasing as you move up the career ladder. 8.2 Other opportunities You may also wish to apply for other sources of money.
